strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor here at Córdoba, especially on this abrasive surface and in this heat.
The pit window is relatively short, so teams will need to nail their stops to avoid losing crucial track position.
Fuel management will be key, especially in the closing stages of the race. Conserving fuel without sacrificing pace is the challenge.
With several heavy braking zones, brake wear will be a concern for many teams. Managing temperatures will be vital.
The historic layout offers a good mix of high-speed corners and tight sections, so finding the right compromise in setup is essential.
A well-timed safety car could really shake things up, presenting a golden opportunity for a strategic gamble.
Running a longer first stint could pay dividends later in the race, but it comes with the risk of getting stuck in traffic.
The teams will be carefully monitoring the wear on the left front tire through Curva 9, one of the toughest corners on the circuit.
